stem: A bank offers a nominal interest rate of 12% per annum, compounded monthly. What is the effective annual rate of interest? [Use: (1.01) raised to the power 12 = 1.1268]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Effective rate = (1 + 0.12/12) raised to the power 12 - 1 = (1.01) raised to the power 12 - 1 = 1.1268 - 1 = 0.1268 = 12.68%.
Student treats the nominal rate as the effective rate, ignoring compounding within the year.
Student uses (1 + 0.12/2)² - 1, treating monthly compounding as semi-annual: (1.06)² - 1 = 0.1236.
Student computes 1.1268 - 1.01 = 0.1168, subtracting one monthly factor instead of 1.

explanation: Effective annual rate = (1 + r/m)^m - 1, where r = 0.12 and m = 12. This gives (1.01) raised to the power 12 - 1 = 1.1268 - 1 = 12.68%. The nominal rate 12% ignores within-year compounding, so it understates the true cost.

explanation_sections.punchline: Monthly compounding means interest earns interest 12 times a year, pushing the effective rate above the 12% nominal figure to 12.68%.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the nominal rate r and the number of compounding periods per year m. Compute the periodic rate r/m. Apply the formula (1 + r/m)^m minus 1. Subtract 1 at the very end, after computing the full power, to get the effective rate as a decimal.
explanation_sections.lesson: The effective rate always exceeds the nominal rate when compounding frequency is greater than once a year. More periods per year means a higher effective rate.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60 seconds. This is an L1 recall item. The stem provides (1.01)^12 = 1.1268. Subtract 1 to get 0.1268 = 12.68%. Reject option (2) in three seconds: 12% is just the nominal rate restated.
